prize_parts.citation: For determining the structure of nitrogenase and its iron-molybdenum cofactor and for the kinetic and spectroscopic framework that explains how the enzyme couples electron transfer and ATP hydrolysis to dinitrogen reduction

statement.case_for: I keep nitrogenase as my first choice, and I want to be precise about why. The prize would rest on what was actually determined: the MoFe protein and FeMo cofactor structures, the interstitial carbide, the ligand- and turnover-state structures from crystallography and cryo-EM, and the kinetic and spectroscopic framework for electron transfer and ATP coupling. These claims have been reproduced by several independent groups over about three decades, and they bear directly on the nitrogen cycle and on ammonia synthesis. The citation I now propose is limited to structure, cofactor chemistry and the established electron-transfer framework, so it does not claim a finished N2 reduction mechanism. That addresses the chair's question on B009: I judge a structure-and-cofactor citation sufficient, because the carbide and cofactor architecture changed the chemical picture of the active site regardless of how the final intermediates are resolved. Rees supplied the decisive crystallographic work, Einsle the atomic-resolution structure that established the central carbide, and Seefeldt the mechanistic kinetics and spectroscopy that interpret the structures.
statement.case_against: The N2 reduction mechanism at the cofactor and its intermediates remain contested, so a wider wording would be a mistake and even the narrow one will be read by some as rewarding structure over mechanism. Credit is crowded: Dean's genetics and biochemistry, and Ribbe's work on cofactor biosynthesis and the isolated cofactor, are serious claims that a three-name cap leaves out. B068 has the broadest support in the committee and a clearer conceptual story, and B003 has the most top-three rankings, so no ballot has a majority and my first choice is not stronger on support than my fallbacks.

responses.point: Nitrogenase should be recognised for its physically grounded structural and mechanistic picture, with Rees, Dean and Seefeldt as the trio, and he discloses that his preference partly reflects his interest in biological energy conversion.
responses.response: We agree on the ballot and on Rees and Seefeldt, and I value that you disclosed your interest. On the third name I still prefer Einsle. The question for a structural citation is who determined what, and Einsle's 2002 high-resolution MoFe structure and the later carbide assignment changed the chemical description of the cofactor. Dean made the protein tractable by genetics, which was essential, but that is enabling work rather than the structure itself. I accept that this is a judgement call, and I would not object if the committee settled on Dean as the compromise, but I would then want the citation to stay on structure and cofactor chemistry so it does not imply a settled mechanism.

responses.point: Targeted protein degradation is a designable, catalytic, event-driven chemical principle, and Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli form the core, with the citation possibly narrowed to the PROTAC concept.
responses.response: I take this seriously, and B068 stays my first alternative. Reproducibility across targets and E3 ligases is real, and the ternary-complex structures from Ciulli's group are the kind of structural evidence I respect. My difficulty is the same one you name: a PROTAC-only citation leaves out the cereblon glue lineage that has the clinical record, and narrowing it to the PROTAC concept makes the prize rest on a modality without an approved drug. I would support B068 over a contested alternative if the committee wants it, but I do not think the lineage question is resolved by choosing three names.

responses.point: A PROTAC-only trio omits the part of the field with the most patient benefit, and if the committee will not separate the two lineages, any three-person split looks arbitrary.
responses.response: I agree with this and it is the strongest argument against B068 as presently configured. The chair asks whether PROTACs and molecular glues are one prize or two. Within a three-name cap I do not see a configuration that credits both lineages honestly, since Handa or Sakamoto would have to displace Ciulli, whose structural work made PROTAC design rational. I think that is a reason to wait, and it is a reason I rank B068 below B009 where the credited work is already settled.

responses.point: Condensates introduced phase separation as a physical-chemical principle of intracellular organisation, mature after fifteen years, with Hyman, Brangwynne and Rosen as the trio.
responses.response: My view of timing is unchanged, and I have moved from dismissing B003 to listing it as an alternative because it has real committee support. Reproduced droplet behaviour in vitro is not in dispute, and Rosen's reconstitution is clean physical chemistry. What I still lack is a structural description of what condensates are at molecular level and agreement on which in vivo cases are true demixing. A citation limited to demixing and multivalency would avoid the in vivo claims, but I doubt it would be much more than a restatement of a well-known physical chemistry principle, and I would then ask why Pappu and Mittag's sequence grammar is not the more quantitative part.

responses.point: Pd-catalysed C-N coupling is a general method with clean two-person attribution and thirty years of confirmation, whose main weakness is its closeness to the 2010 prize.
responses.response: The attribution and maturity argument is strong, and I agree that C-N coupling is mechanistically distinct from the C-C reactions recognised in 2010 because the bottleneck is reductive elimination from amido complexes. I do not rank it above B009 because I judge the 2010 overlap to be a heavier burden for a method than for a structural problem, and because the opening rankings show little support for it. I would not object to it as a fallback in a deadlocked vote.

uncertainties: Whether the committee accepts a nitrogenase prize built on structure and cofactor chemistry while the N2 reduction mechanism remains unresolved.
Whether Einsle or Dean should be named beside Rees and Seefeldt, and how Ribbe's claim should be weighed.
Whether B068 can be configured without an arbitrary split between the PROTAC and molecular-glue lineages, and how a later clinical approval would change my view.
statement.conflict_note: Clarification of round 1: B009 is my first choice and my stated configuration. My reference to B033 as my own first choice was an error, and I now list B068 and B003 as alternatives. I have no personal tie to any candidate on the shortlist. I am a Stockholm University colleague of the Secretary, Peter Brzezinski, who also supports B009, but this is not a personal tie to any candidate. My own work on electron crystallography and 3D electron diffraction does not involve nitrogenase.
